_comment: Shared truth for the board mapping, the vote threshold and the working-day windows. Read by app/tests/governance-fixture.test.ts, app/tests/board.test.ts, app/tests/nominations.test.ts and tools/tests/test_governance_fixture.py. A case added here must pass in both languages.

active_board_cases.name: an active member with no declared absence is eligible
an inactive member leaves the board entirely, not merely the eligible set
a member away until a future date is unavailable but stays on the board
a member whose absence has lapsed is available again the day after
the boundary day itself is still an absence - unavailable_until is inclusive
an empty unavailable_until declares no absence at all
a malformed unavailable_until reads as an absence rather than as availability
a whole board at once: active, inactive, future, lapsed, boundary, empty, malformed

threshold_cases.name: board of 3 needs 3 - the floor overrides the ratio
board of 6 needs 4 - the handbook's own example
board of 9 needs 6 - the handbook's other example

decision_cases.name: four yes on a board of six is decided
abstentions stay in the denominator, so three yes is not enough
recusals leave the denominator, lowering the bar
declared unavailability leaves the denominator too
too few eligible members suspends the vote instead of lowering the bar
the absolute floor of three yes holds even when the ratio is met
a repeated yes ballot from the same voter counts once, not twice

assign_lead_cases.name: the eligible member carrying fewer open leads is chosen
a tie on open leads goes to whichever member's most recent assignment is oldest
a member who declared an absence covering today is skipped for one who did not
an inactive member is skipped even while carrying no leads
a board with no available member returns an empty string rather than throwing

_unsettled_comment: Whether the board still has a nomination in front of it. app/src/state/board.ts::isUnsettled refuses a second nomination for the candidate while this is true, and tools/convener_ops/sweep.py::_unsettled_candidates keeps that same candidate off the inactivity proposal. One rule, two implementations, so both read these cases: the Python copy mirrored the narrower isPending until this fixture was written, and a seated member carrying a deferred nomination could be proposed inactive out of the very file that recorded the objection against them. `unsettled` is what isUnsettled returns for `nomination`; the Python side reads the same cases through _unsettled_candidates, which is this predicate applied to a list.

unsettled_nomination_cases.name: a nomination with no outcome yet is unsettled: the board has not answered
a waiting nomination is unsettled: the rule is met and only a seat is missing
an accepted nomination is settled for good
a deferred nomination whose objection still stands is unsettled
a deferred nomination with no objection left on it is settled: there is nothing to withdraw
an objection standing on a nomination with no outcome keeps it unsettled

objections.reason: I want to write to the candidate first.

unsettled_nomination_cases.name: a waiting nomination carrying an objection is unsettled twice over

objections.reason: Not while the seat question is open.

working_day_cases._comment: Working-day arithmetic, pinned across app/src/state/working-days.ts and tools/convener_ops/governance.py. Weekends are Saturday and Sunday. PUBLIC HOLIDAYS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED: the board's members do not share one national calendar, so a holiday list right for France would be wrong for the others, and an unmodelled holiday only ever makes a window longer, which is the prudent direction. The 1 May 2026 cases below pin that as a decision rather than an oversight. The count is of the days AFTER the start day, and `elapsed` is the exact inverse of `add`.

add.name: three working days from a Monday land on the Thursday
three working days from a Thursday cross the weekend and land on the Tuesday
three working days from a Friday land on the Wednesday
three working days from a Saturday land on the same Wednesday as from the Friday
three working days from a Sunday land on that Wednesday too
one working day from a Friday is the Monday
zero working days is the identity
zero working days from a Saturday is that Saturday, not the Monday
1 May 2026 is counted as an ordinary Friday - holidays are not modelled

elapsed.name: Monday to Thursday is three working days
Thursday to the following Tuesday is three working days, the weekend uncounted
Friday to Monday is one working day
Saturday to Monday is one working day
a span inside the weekend is zero working days
the same day is zero working days
a full week is five working days
the 1 May 2026 span counts three working days, holidays included as ordinary days

_board_headcount_comment: board_min and board_max count *active* members, on both sides. app/src/state/board.ts::resolveNominations counts them before seating and tools/convener_ops/validate.py::validate_config checks the same number, so the app cannot write a config its own validator rejects. G-07's floor and ceiling are about who can vote, and an inactive entry is out of the denominator.

board_headcount_cases.name: a board of three active members sits on its floor
an inactive entry does not occupy a seat
four inactive entries still leave a board of five on its ceiling
a tenth active member is over the ceiling
two active members are under the floor whatever else is on file
an unavailable member still holds their seat

_identifier_comment: What a decision commit may point at. `_TOKEN` in tools/convener_ops/commit_format.py and `TOKEN` in app/src/state/decisions.ts are the same rule, read from both sides here. A record, never a person by name: a commit subject is permanent and unrewritable, so a name typed into a nomination box would be there for good.

identifier_cases.name: a speaker reference is an identifier
a github login is an identifier
the board as a whole is an identifier
a login with a hyphen is an identifier
a login with a dot and an underscore is an identifier
a digit may open an identifier
a person's name is not an identifier - it is prose about a person
a name with an affiliation is not an identifier
a leading space is not an identifier
a trailing space is not an identifier
an identifier may not open with punctuation
an email address is not an identifier
a second line is not an identifier
the word by is not allowed to hide inside one

_lateness_comment: The overdue wording, pinned across the two languages. app/src/state/sla.ts renders these sentences on the screens and tools/convener_ops/notify.py puts the same ones in the daily digest (spec section 7): one sentence, two readers, so a reword that reaches only one side fails here. `state` is the arm of sla.ts's Lateness; `days`, `overdue_text` and `waiting_since` exist on the overdue arm only, because a step that is not late has no day count to render. Deadlines are counted in calendar days -- the fourteen-day case spanning two weekends is here so that reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

lateness_cases.name: a lead past its board-decision deadline is overdue by whole calendar days
one day late reads in the singular
the due day itself is still within the target, not yet late
fourteen calendar days, so a window spanning two weekends still falls due on the same Friday
a lead with no recorded opening day has no deadline rather than a guessed one
an invited record counts thirty days from the day the decision was recorded
a delivered talk missing both artefacts reports the earlier of the two deadlines
once the summary is in, its deadline stops existing and the recording is what is waiting
a delivered talk with both artefacts in has no deadline left at all
a confirmed record is waiting on no policy deadline
